```python
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("JSSP")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_jobs = 11
    n_machines = 3
    processing_times = [[25, 27, 30], [19, 16, 22], [16, 19, 7], [24, 11, 6], [22, 22, 21], [19, 11, 29], [24, 8, 13], [30, 19, 29], [18, 12, 19], [17, 22, 10], [14, 21, 30]]
    machine_assignments = [[0, 2, 1], [0, 2, 1], [2, 1, 0], [2, 0, 1], [2, 1, 0], [1, 2, 0], [1, 2, 0], [1, 0, 2], [0, 1, 2], [0, 1, 2], [2, 0, 1]]

    # Big-M: sum of all processing times
    M = sum(processing_times[j][o] for j in range(n_jobs) for o in range(n_machines))

    # --- Variables ---
    # Start times for each operation
    S = {}
    for j in range(n_jobs):
        for o in range(n_machines):
            S[(j,o)] = m.addVar(lb=0, ub=M, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Start_{j}_{o}")

    # Makespan variable
    Cmax = m.addVar(lb=0, ub=M, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="Cmax")

    # Build machine -> [(job, op)] mapping
    machine_ops = {mach: [] for mach in range(n_machines)}
    for j in range(n_jobs):
        for o in range(n_machines):
            machine_ops[machine_assignments[j][o]].append((j, o))

    # Disjunctive binary variables for each pair on same machine
    Y = {}
    for mach in range(n_machines):
        ops = machine_ops[mach]
        for i in range(len(ops)):
            for k in range(i+1, len(ops)):
                j1, o1 = ops[i]
                j2, o2 = ops[k]
                Y[(j1,o1,j2,o2)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Y_{j1}_{o1}_{j2}_{o2}")

    # --- Objective: minimize makespan ---
    m.setObjective(Cmax, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Precedence: operations within a job must follow order
    for j in range(n_jobs):
        for o in range(n_machines - 1):
            m.addConstr(
                S[(j,o+1)] >= S[(j,o)] + processing_times[j][o],
                name=f"Prec_{j}_{o}")

    # 2. Disjunctive: no two operations on the same machine overlap
    for mach in range(n_machines):
        ops = machine_ops[mach]
        for i in range(len(ops)):
            for k in range(i+1, len(ops)):
                j1, o1 = ops[i]
                j2, o2 = ops[k]
                p1 = processing_times[j1][o1]
                p2 = processing_times[j2][o2]
                y = Y[(j1,o1,j2,o2)]
                m.addConstr(
                    S[(j1,o1)] + p1 <= S[(j2,o2)] + M * (1 - y),
                    name=f"Disj_A_{j1}_{o1}_{j2}_{o2}")
                m.addConstr(
                    S[(j2,o2)] + p2 <= S[(j1,o1)] + M * y,
                    name=f"Disj_B_{j1}_{o1}_{j2}_{o2}")

    # 3. Makespan: Cmax >= completion of last operation of each job
    for j in range(n_jobs):
        last_op = n_machines - 1
        m.addConstr(
            Cmax >= S[(j, last_op)] + processing_times[j][last_op],
            name=f"Makespan_J{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Plant Leadership and Scheduling Team
From: Manufacturing Operations Manager
Subject: Coordinated Scheduling of Jobs Across Specialized Workstations

Context
Our facility processes a defined set of customer orders through multiple specialized workstations. Each job follows a predetermined routing, consisting of a fixed sequence of operations. Every operation is executed on a specific machine for a known duration. While individual tasks are straightforward, coordinating them across the shop floor is complex because different jobs share the same machines at different points in their routings.

Scheduling Challenge
The core challenge is to decide the order in which each machine processes its queued operations so that:
- Machines remain productively utilized without creating bottlenecks.
- Jobs arrive at subsequent steps when capacity is available, avoiding excessive waiting.
- Work does not pile up ahead of heavily used machines while other machines are idle.
Because jobs intersect on common machines at different times, sequencing choices on one workstation affect queues and completion times on others. The combined effect of these local choices determines when the final job finishes.

Operating Rules and Requirements
- Fixed job routing: Operations within a job must be completed in the defined order; later steps cannot begin until prior steps finish.
- Machine specificity: Each operation is assigned to a particular machine, and that assignment cannot be changed.
- Known durations: The processing time for every operation is established in advance.
- Machine exclusivity: A machine can handle only one operation at a time; overlapping work on the same machine is not allowed.
- No preemption: Once an operation starts on a machine, it runs to completion without interruption.

Goal
Build a feasible, conflict-free timeline for all operations across all machines that respects the rules above and completes the full set of jobs in the shortest possible overall time (makespan). Practically, this means selecting the processing order at each machine so that the time when the last job finishes is minimized, while keeping machines well utilized and avoiding unnecessary idle time or waiting between steps.

Next Steps
The scheduling team will use the attached production data—machine assignments and processing times by operation—to evaluate sequencing options on each workstation. The intent is to produce a shop-wide schedule that meets the rules and achieves the shortest total completion time. Any proposed schedule will be reviewed for feasibility, clarity of handoffs between machines, and ease of execution on the floor.

Annex – Production Data
- Number of jobs: 11
- Number of machines (workstations): 3
- Job-by-job production schedule (operations must be performed in the listed sequence):
  Job 10: Op1 on Machine 0 for 17 time units → Op2 on Machine 1 for 22 time units → Op3 on Machine 2 for 10 time units
